name: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge
image_query: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge Annapurna view
summary: A small, quiet luxury lodge of stone cottages on a ridge about 10 km east of Pokhara, facing the full Annapurna range and Machhapuchhre. Guided village walks, birding, yoga and massage replace town noise. Our first choice for honeymoon and luxury stays near Pokhara.
body: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge opened in the late 1990s on a forested ridge above the Pokhara valley, built from local stone and slate in the style of a hill village. It has only around 18 rooms, set in cottages with private verandas facing either the mountains or the valley. The main lodge holds a lounge with a fireplace, a dining room serving set menus that use produce from the garden and local farms, and a terrace that looks straight across to Machhapuchhre and the Annapurnas.

Days here are slow by design. Lodge naturalists lead bird walks in the surrounding forest and hikes to nearby villages, and there is an outdoor pool on the ridge with the mountains as the backdrop. Yoga, meditation and Ayurvedic and other massages can be booked, and the lodge arranges paragliding, ultralight flights and Lakeside visits for those who want them. The lodge is known for its work with nearby communities and its sustainable approach. Rates are usually full board.
why: Uninterrupted views of Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range from the rooms and pool
Small size and hilltop setting mean silence, privacy and no traffic
Guided walks, birding, yoga and massage included or easy to arrange on site

faqs.q: How far is Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge from Lakeside?
faqs.a: The lodge is on a ridge about 10 km east of Pokhara, roughly 30–40 minutes by car from Lakeside, with the last section on a hill road. The lodge arranges transfers from the airport and town. It is ideal if you want peace and mountain views rather than walking to Lakeside restaurants every evening.

faqs.q: Is Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. With around 18 rooms in stone cottages, private verandas facing the Annapurnas, a ridge-top pool and quiet evenings by the fire, it is one of the most romantic places to stay near Pokhara. We pair it with a night or two at Lakeside for boating and restaurants.

faqs.q: Are children allowed at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge?
faqs.a: Families are welcome, and older children enjoy the nature walks and pool, but the lodge is designed for quiet, so it suits calm families rather than those with toddlers. Some cottages are reached by paths and steps. Check current age policies and family room options when you book.

name: Fish Tail Lodge
image_query: Fish Tail Lodge Phewa Lake raft
summary: Pokhara's original lake resort, opened in 1969 on a wooded peninsula in Phewa Lake and reached only by a hand-pulled raft. Gardens, a pool and lake-facing rooms look across the water to Machhapuchhre, yet central Lakeside is a few minutes away.
body: Fish Tail Lodge stands on a small peninsula at the southern end of Phewa Lake, opposite the Basundhara area and close to Damside. Guests cross a short stretch of water on a flat pontoon raft pulled by hand along a rope, which sets the tone: once across, there are no cars, only gardens, trees and the lake on three sides. The lodge was the first resort-style hotel in Pokhara when it opened in 1969, and its round, low-rise buildings have been renovated over the years.

There are about 60 rooms, many facing the lake and the mountains, with an outdoor swimming pool, a children's pool, a restaurant and bar and lawns that run down to the water. The view across Phewa to Machhapuchhre and the Annapurnas on clear mornings is the main draw, and the World Peace Pagoda is directly across the lake. Cultural dance evenings are held on some nights. Boating, birdwatching and Lakeside are all close at hand.
why: Lake on three sides and Machhapuchhre in view from the garden and many rooms
Car-free peninsula reached by rope raft, quiet but minutes from Lakeside
Pool and lawns suit families, while history and setting suit couples

faqs.q: How do you get to Fish Tail Lodge?
faqs.a: Cars drop you at the lodge's landing on the lakeshore near Basundhara and Damside, and you cross to the peninsula on a hand-pulled pontoon raft in a couple of minutes. Staff carry luggage across. The raft runs whenever guests need it, including in the evening.

faqs.q: Is Fish Tail Lodge suitable for elderly guests?
faqs.a: Yes. The raft crossing is short and staff help guests on and off, and the grounds are mostly level with garden paths. Ask for a ground-floor, lake-facing room. Avoid crossing in heavy storms. It is a peaceful choice for seniors who want a lake view without traffic.

faqs.q: Can you see the mountains from Fish Tail Lodge?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. The lodge looks north across Phewa Lake to Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range, with the reflection on the water in still morning conditions. Views are clearest from October to March. Lake-facing rooms and the garden have the best outlook.

name: Temple Tree Resort & Spa
image_query: Temple Tree Resort Spa Pokhara pool
summary: A boutique resort at Gaurighat in Lakeside, built in stone and timber around a garden pool and named after the frangipani, or temple tree. It has two restaurants and a full spa, and Phewa Lake is a three-minute walk away. A favourite for couples.
body: Temple Tree Resort & Spa sits in a quiet lane at Gaurighat, at the northern end of central Lakeside, a few minutes' walk from the shore of Phewa Lake and about 15 minutes on foot from the Tal Barahi boat ghat. Its architecture draws on the stone, slate and carved wood of the western Nepal hills, with low buildings arranged around a landscaped garden and an outdoor swimming pool shaded by frangipani trees.

Rooms are styled with local stone, wood and textiles, and some have balconies facing the garden or the hills. There are two restaurants serving Nepali, Indian and continental food, a bar and a full-service spa offering massages and Ayurvedic treatments, which makes it a good base for honeymoon and wellness itineraries. It combines the convenience of Lakeside, with restaurants, boating and paragliding offices nearby, with a calmer atmosphere than the main strip.
why: Garden pool and full spa within a short walk of Phewa Lake
Boutique design in local stone and timber, calmer than the main Lakeside strip
Two restaurants, plus Lakeside dining and boating on the doorstep

faqs.q: Where is Temple Tree Resort & Spa in Pokhara?
faqs.a: It is at Gaurighat, Lakeside, in a side lane near the northern end of the central Lakeside area. Phewa Lake is about a three-minute walk away, and the Tal Barahi boat ghat around 15 minutes on foot. Restaurants, shops and adventure booking offices are all within walking distance.

faqs.q: Does Temple Tree have a swimming pool and spa?
faqs.a: Yes. The resort has an outdoor swimming pool in its central garden and a full-service spa offering massages, body treatments and Ayurvedic therapies. Spa treatments are charged separately. Our honeymoon and yoga packages often include a spa session here. Book treatments in advance in peak months.

faqs.q: Is Temple Tree good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The garden and pool are popular with children, it is in a quieter lane than the main Lakeside road, and the lake and boats are a short walk away. Ask for interconnecting or family room options when booking. It suits families wanting comfort without a large, busy hotel.

name: Hotel Barahi
summary: A long-established Lakeside hotel beside Phewa Lake with an outdoor pool, garden, Ayurvedic spa and Nepali cultural dance evenings. Comfortable, central and good value, it is our standard choice for families and first-time visitors on Pokhara packages.
body: Hotel Barahi is in the heart of Lakeside, a short walk from the Barahi ghat where boats leave for Tal Barahi temple, and close to restaurants, shops and the paragliding and rafting offices. Rooms are arranged in several wings around a garden and an outdoor swimming pool, a real advantage in Pokhara's warm afternoons and a big draw for families with children. Lakeside's lakeshore promenade is only a few minutes away.

Rooms are air-conditioned with cable TV and private bathrooms, in a range of categories from standard to deluxe, some with partial lake or mountain views. The hotel has a restaurant serving Nepali, Indian and continental food, a wellness spa offering Ayurvedic treatments, and evening performances of Nepali cultural dances in the garden on many nights. It is a practical, friendly base for a three- or four-night stay that keeps everything within walking distance.
why: Central Lakeside location near the Tal Barahi boat ghat
Outdoor pool and garden, rare at this price level and ideal for children
Ayurvedic spa and cultural dance evenings on site

faqs.q: Is Hotel Barahi close to Phewa Lake?
faqs.a: Yes. It is in central Lakeside, a short walk from the Barahi boat ghat for Tal Barahi temple, and close to the lakeshore promenade, restaurants and shops. Most sightseeing pick-ups are from the hotel door. It is one of the most convenient addresses for first-time visitors.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Barahi have a swimming pool?
faqs.a: Yes, an outdoor swimming pool in the garden, popular with families from March to October when afternoons are warm. Check pool hours and any seasonal closures with the hotel. A children's area and garden seating surround it. Towels are provided at the poolside.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Barahi good for Indian families?
faqs.a: Yes. It is central, has a pool and garden for children, serves Indian vegetarian dishes alongside Nepali and continental food, and can arrange Jain meals with notice. Family and connecting rooms are available on request. It is a common choice on our family packages.

name: Pokhara Grande
summary: Pokhara's largest five-star hotel, at Birauta Chowk in Pardi near Damside, with about 140 rooms and suites, a large pool, several restaurants and bars, a spa and gym. It suits families and travellers who want full-service luxury, about eight minutes' walk from the lake.
body: Pokhara Grande stands at Birauta Chowk in the Pardi area, south of Lakeside and close to Damside and the southern end of Phewa Lake, about an eight-minute walk from the water. It is a large, modern hotel with around 140 rooms and suites, many with views towards the mountains or the city, and it hosts conferences and weddings as well as leisure travellers. The airport is about 15–20 minutes by road.

Facilities are the most complete in Pokhara: a large outdoor swimming pool, four restaurants and bars, Spa Pavitra offering Thai massage, Ayurvedic treatments and facials, a gym, shopping arcade and travel desk. Rooms have twin or king beds, climate control, minibar, tea and coffee makers and Wi-Fi. For travellers who want a big-hotel experience with everything on site, and for families who value a pool and choice of restaurants, it is the obvious choice.
why: Full five-star facilities: large pool, spa, gym and four restaurants and bars
Close to Damside and Phewa Lake, with easy road access to the airport and Peace Pagoda
Spacious rooms and suites suited to families and groups

faqs.q: Is Pokhara Grande a five-star hotel?
faqs.a: Yes. Pokhara Grande is a five-star hotel with about 140 rooms and suites, a large outdoor pool, spa, gym and four restaurants and bars. It is the largest full-service luxury hotel in the city and is used on our Pokhara luxury and family packages.

faqs.q: How far is Pokhara Grande from Lakeside?
faqs.a: The hotel is at Birauta Chowk, Pardi, about an eight-minute walk from the southern end of Phewa Lake near Damside, and around 10 minutes by taxi from central Lakeside. The airport is about 15–20 minutes away by road. Taxis wait at the hotel entrance.

faqs.q: Does Pokhara Grande have mountain views?
faqs.a: Many rooms face north towards the Annapurna range and Machhapuchhre, which are visible on clear days from October to March. Ask for a mountain-view room at booking. City-facing rooms are cheaper. The rooftop and pool areas also give views on clear mornings.

name: The Old Inn
image_query: The Old Inn Bandipur Newari house
summary: A heritage guesthouse in two restored Newar townhouses, about 150 and 250 years old, on Bandipur's car-free main street. Original brickwork and carved wooden windows, around 20 rooms, a dining room on the bazaar and a back terrace facing the Himalaya.
body: The Old Inn occupies two neighbouring houses on the stone-paved main street of Bandipur, restored to keep their red brick walls, carved wooden doorways, lattice windows and low beamed ceilings. One wing is roughly 150 years old and the other about 250, from the era when Bandipur was a prosperous stop on the trade route between India and Tibet. Rooms, about 20 in all, are spread over three floors, each different in size and shape, with en suite bathrooms; some look out over the Himalaya, others over the bazaar.

Meals mix Nepali and continental dishes and are served in a dining room opening onto the street or on a quieter terrace at the back with mountain views on clear days. Breakfast is included. Staying here lets you enjoy Bandipur after the day visitors have gone: sunset at the tundikhel, an evening stroll along the lantern-lit street and sunrise from the terrace. Stairs are steep and narrow, as in all old Newar houses.
why: Authentic restored Newar townhouses on Bandipur's car-free bazaar
Back terrace with Himalayan views on clear mornings
Steps from the tundikhel, Thani Mai trail and Bindebasini temple

faqs.q: Is The Old Inn Bandipur suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. The house has steep, narrow wooden stairs typical of old Newar buildings, so ask for a lower-floor room. The bazaar itself is flat and car-free. Porters carry luggage from the car park at the entrance to the bazaar, a few minutes' walk.

faqs.q: Do rooms at The Old Inn have mountain views?
faqs.a: Some do. Rooms vary in size and outlook: some face the Himalaya across the valley, others look over the bazaar street. Mountain-view rooms are limited, so request one early. The back terrace has a view for everyone on clear days.

faqs.q: Can cars reach The Old Inn?
faqs.a: No. Bandipur's main bazaar is closed to vehicles. Cars park at the entrance to the town, a few minutes' walk away, and hotel staff carry luggage. This keeps the street quiet and safe, and is part of the town's charm.
